specification.problem: Decide whether two n-qubit circuits U and V (or their output states) are equivalent up to global phase using a swap test, for a tiny explicit instance. This is a generic dense-simulation realisation; the paper's scalable algorithms are not recovered.
specification.reconstruction_scope: n=2 instance with U = H on qubit 0 then CNOT(0,1) (Bell preparation), and V either identical to U or a variant with a relative phase (e.g. U followed by Z on qubit 0). State-equivalence swap test on |0^n> inputs, built as a measurement-free unitary. The Choi-state variant and the controlled-U/V† exact-phase variant are described but not the primary built circuit. Excluded: the paper's scalable algorithms for hundreds of qubits, its equivalence taxonomy, and the teleportation and Grover benchmarks.

symbols.domain: positive integer, n=2 in the instance

symbols.meaning: unitaries on n qubits, compiled explicitly into gates
probability of ancilla outcome 0 after the swap test

equations.label: Equivalence up to global phase
equations.description: Equality up to global phase is equivalent to unit overlap. This is the Cauchy-Schwarz equality condition for unit vectors.
equations.justification: Cauchy-Schwarz equality case. The abstract only says that several notions of equivalence exist.

equations.label: Swap test probability
equations.description: Probability of the ancilla being 0 after H, controlled-SWAP(A,B), H, with A and B holding |psi_U> and |psi_V>.
assumptions: Ancilla, A and B start in |0>
U acts on A and V acts on B

equations.label: Swap test unitary
equations.description: Measurement-free unitary on 1+2n qubits. Applied to |0>, it yields p_0 from eq_2.
equations.justification: Proposed construction from the method plan, not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Ancilla is qubit 0, then A, then B

equations.label: Choi-state version
equations.description: Applying the swap test to the Choi states of U and V tests circuit equivalence up to global phase, since the overlap equals 1 iff V = e^{i theta} U.
equations.justification: Choi-Jamiolkowski overlap identity. This is an extension, not the primary built circuit.
assumptions: Reference registers R_A and R_B are swapped alongside A and B

equations.label: Exact equality with global phase
equations.description: Hadamard test on the ancilla, with controlled-U and controlled-V† on A. It equals 1 iff U|0>=V|0> exactly, including global phase.
equations.justification: Standard Hadamard-test form for the variant described in the plan. It is not built in the primary scope.
assumptions: Controlled-U and controlled-V† applied between the two Hadamards

registers.name: R_A,R_B
registers.role: reference registers for the Choi construction, not in the primary build

specification.initial_state: |0>_a|0^n>_A|0^n>_B, qubit order a,A,B, little-endian integer encoding as in Qiskit

steps.description: Apply U to A and V to B, where U = H(q0) then CNOT(q0,q1), and V = U or U followed by Z on q0.
Apply H on the ancilla, then CSWAP controlled by the ancilla for each qubit pair of A and B, then H on the ancilla.
Decode in the simulator: compute P(a=0) from the statevector. Declare equivalent up to global phase if P(a=0) >= 1-epsilon.

specification.measurement: No in-circuit measurement. The simulator reads the ancilla-0 probability from the statevector.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Declare equivalence up to global phase if p_0 is within epsilon of 1; otherwise declare non-equivalence.
assumptions: The tiny instance with n=2 and the gate choices for U and V are assumptions.
U and V are compiled explicitly, so no black-box query claim is made.
Only the global-phase-insensitive state-equivalence test is the primary build.
missing_information: The paper's actual algorithms, such as decision-diagram or stabilizer-style methods.
The paper's taxonomy of equivalence notions.
